tasks.short: Run training sessions on site: toolbox talks, role plays for team leads, onboarding classes, safety refreshers.

today.trigger: A scheduled session in the Studytube calendar, an onboarding wave, or a manager asking for a team session.
steps: Prepare slides, cases and role-play scripts from earlier sessions
Book a room or warehouse floor slot around shift times
Deliver the session in person or on Teams and run exercises
Handle questions, often in mixed Dutch, English and Polish groups
Record attendance in Studytube
drudgery: Rewriting the same role-play cases for each group
Re-typing paper attendance lists into Studytube
today.time_sinks: Preparing fresh cases and exercises per audience, and repeating the same sessions per shift and per site.

lenses.faster: Case and role-play scripts per group are drafted in minutes and attendance is captured with a QR scan; the session itself takes as long as before, so about 15% of the task disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Little runs alone: a session booked in Studytube triggers a prep pack draft (cases, discussion questions, translated handouts) that the specialist edits before the session.
lenses.ambitious: Team leads on night shifts get an AI practice partner for difficult conversations (absence talks, feedback) between sessions, a group served for the first time; demand would grow as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rewriting cases and typing attendance; the specialist wants more time facilitating discussion and coaching on the floor.
lenses.options: Two or three versions of a case (warehouse, transport, office) let the specialist pick the one closest to the group's real situation.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from preparing to facilitating and coaching team leads; the specialist decides which practice tools team leads use and becomes more expert in facilitation.
reach: HR Business Partner: coaching team leads on absence conversations under Wet verbetering poortwachter; needs grounding in poortwachter steps

tasks.human_edge: Reading the room, handling resistance from experienced drivers, adjusting on the spot, and building trust with shift workers; practical safety training stays human.
tasks.pattern_why: Delivery is live and with people; AI only helps prepare and lets learners practise, the trainer stays the lead.

in_practice.trigger: A session is scheduled in Studytube.
steps: Model drafts cases, role-play scripts and discussion questions for the audience
Specialist edits and translates key handouts
Specialist delivers the session
Attendance captured via QR into Studytube
Optional AI practice partner, disclosed as AI, for team leads after the session
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist chooses and edits all material and runs the session; the practice partner is clearly labelled as AI (Art. 50).
data_needed: Past cases and session notes from SharePoint

evidence.claim: An agent drafting manager feedback against the SBI rubric raised write-up quality 16 points for users versus 7 for non-users.
An AI assistant raised novice productivity 34% in customer support.
An AI tutor must disclose it is AI; inferring learner emotions from webcam is banned.

risks: Learners delegate practice to AI and learn less
A practice tool that logs team-lead performance becomes monitoring and needs works council consent (WOR 27(1)(l))
Translations of safety terms are wrong
research_questions: Do team leads who use an AI practice partner hold better absence conversations, judged by HRBPs, after three months?
How many hours per month go into case preparation today versus delivery?
Will the works council accept a practice tool if no individual results are stored?

tasks.short: Make handouts, e-learnings, work instructions and onboarding guides, mostly in Studytube and PowerPoint.

today.trigger: A new process, policy or CAO change, a site manager request, or an outdated course in Studytube.
steps: Collect source material from SharePoint policies, SOPs and subject experts
Write the outline and text
Build slides, handouts or a Studytube module with quiz questions
Get the subject expert or safety lead to check it
Publish and file in Studytube and SharePoint
drudgery: Turning long SOP documents into short steps
today.time_sinks: First drafts and chasing subject experts for review.

lenses.faster: Studytube AI Authoring drafts the outline, text and quiz from the SOP PDF; the specialist edits, checks reading level and gets sign-off, cutting about half the task time.
lenses.autonomous: An updated SOP or policy in SharePoint triggers a draft course update in Studytube; nothing is published until the specialist approves and the safety lead signs safety content.
lenses.ambitious: Flex workers from the three agencies get short, translated first-shift instructions per site and job, a group served for the first time; demand would grow with lower cost.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses writing quiz questions or condensing SOPs; the specialist wants more time with operations getting the content right.
lenses.options: Two drafts at different reading levels or formats (one-page card versus five-minute module) can be tested with a team lead before choosing.
lenses.altitude: The specialist moves from producing content to owning the content catalogue and the review standard, and decides when a course is retired; the job becomes more editorial and more expert.
reach: HR Administrator: onboarding letters and first-day information packs; needs knowledge of AFAS contract data
Recruiter: job-specific realistic job previews for vacancies

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what actually happens on the warehouse floor, spotting unsafe or wrong steps, and choosing what to leave out.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns a source document into a checkable draft inside a fixed author-review-publish workflow.

in_practice.trigger: A new or changed SOP, policy or course request lands in the SharePoint L&D intake list.
steps: Upload the source document to Studytube AI Authoring
Model drafts outline, text and quiz questions
Model checks reading level and produces an English version
Specialist edits; safety lead signs safety content
Publish in Studytube with source and version noted
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves every course; safety lead signs safety content before publishing.
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube course version history and SharePoint intake list

evidence.claim: Studytube AI Authoring drafts outlines, scripts and questions from a title or uploaded PDF, PPT or SCORM; authors edit.
MHR's learning team has an agent draft content and check reading level, with a person reviewing.
Workers spend 42% of AI time troubleshooting output.

risks: Errors in safety steps published without real expert review
Editing AI drafts takes longer than expected
Content grows faster than anyone can maintain it
research_questions: How long does a Studytube AI draft take to fix for a real Noordhaven SOP, timed on three courses?
Do flex workers given translated first-shift cards have fewer incidents or errors in week one?
How many active courses lack an owner or review date today?

tasks.short: Run the training offer: mandatory certificates (forklift, VCA, food safety), refreshers and skills courses per site.

today.trigger: A certificate about to expire, a new hire, a manager request, or the yearly training plan.
steps: Export certificate expiry dates from Studytube into Excel
Match against AFAS rosters and staffing agency lists
Book external providers for forklift and VCA exams
Enrol staff and send invites around shifts
Chase no-shows and rebook
drudgery: Matching names between Studytube, AFAS and agency lists
today.time_sinks: Manual matching of expiry dates to shift rosters and chasing attendance.

lenses.faster: A nightly job matches Studytube expiry dates to AFAS rosters and proposes bookings; the specialist handles exceptions, removing about 35% of the task.
lenses.autonomous: A certificate 90 days from expiry starts the run: the system enrols the worker on a session that fits their roster and notifies them and their team lead; the specialist handles conflicts and provider bookings.
lenses.ambitious: Every flex worker is certified before their first shift, checked at agency order time, a group served for the first time; demand would grow as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the expiry spreadsheet; the specialist wants more time on which skills programmes actually reduce errors and turnover.
lenses.options: Few; when a session is short of seats, scenarios on which teams to prioritise help the site manager decide.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the competence record for all three sites and decides certification priorities with site managers; less admin, more expert.
reach: HR Administrator: certificate data in AFAS personnel files
Staffing agency coordination: checking flex worker certificates at order time; needs agency portal access and contract terms

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating with site managers about releasing people from shifts, judging exceptions, and dealing with external exam providers.
tasks.pattern_why: Expiry rules, roster matching and booking can be written down and run without a model.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly run finds a certificate expiring within 90 days or a new hire without a mandatory certificate.
steps: Pull expiry dates from Studytube and rosters from AFAS
Propose a session that fits the worker's shifts
Enrol and notify worker and team lead
Flag conflicts and missing sessions to the specialist
Report certified-on-first-shift rate in Power BI
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist handles exceptions and provider bookings; outside bodies certify forklift and VCA.
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube enrolment log and a Power BI exceptions report

evidence.claim: Certificate expiry, enrolment and scheduling suit deterministic software using Studytube expiry dates plus AFAS rosters.
Outside bodies certify VCA and forklift skills; AI only prepares learners.

risks: Name and ID mismatches between AFAS, Studytube and agency lists
Auto-enrolment ignores operational peaks
Flex worker data shared across systems without an AVG basis
research_questions: What share of shift staff start a shift with an expired or missing mandatory certificate today?
Can the AFAS and Studytube APIs give a reliable shared employee key?
Do agencies share certificate data per worker, and under which AVG agreement?

tasks.short: Track who did which training and check if programmes work, using evaluations and Power BI reports.

today.trigger: End of a course, month-end report, or a manager or HR Director asking whether a programme works.
steps: Export completions and evaluation scores from Studytube
Read and tag open comments by hand
Combine with AFAS data in Excel or Power BI
Write a short report for HR management
drudgery: Rebuilding the same Excel each month
today.time_sinks: Manual tagging of comments and stitching data together.

lenses.faster: Power BI shows completions and outcomes automatically and a model clusters comments; the specialist checks themes and writes the conclusion, saving about 40%.
lenses.autonomous: Course close triggers comment clustering and a draft summary at group level; the specialist reviews before anything goes to management.
lenses.ambitious: Measure every onboarding programme against week-one onboarding completion and 90-day retention per site, a decision made far more often than today; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses tagging comments; the specialist wants more time agreeing measures with managers up front.
lenses.options: Comparing two programme versions by site or shift shows which to keep.
lenses.altitude: The specialist decides which measures count and agrees them with managers before launch; more analytical and more expert.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: Power BI training dashboards; needs DAX and data model basics

tasks.human_edge: Choosing measures that matter, knowing what else changed on a site, and keeping results at group level.
tasks.pattern_why: Reports are deterministic in Power BI; one model call clusters open comments into checkable themes.

in_practice.trigger: A course or cohort closes, or monthly report run.
steps: Power BI refreshes completion and outcome data
Model clusters open comments into themes with example quotes
Specialist checks themes against raw comments
Specialist writes conclusion and shares group-level report
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves every report; no individual data goes into appraisals.
data_needed: Onboarding and 90-day retention data from AFAS

evidence.claim: MHR agrees measures with managers first, collects at six weeks and six months, and uses AI to cluster comments, not to decide.
From 2 December 2027 AI using learning data to evaluate workers is high-risk.
Workday advises setting baselines before launch.

risks: Individual learning data creeps into appraisals, making it high-risk and needing works council consent
Clusters miss minority complaints
Correlation read as programme effect
research_questions: Can AFAS give onboarding and 90-day retention by cohort and site?
How well do model clusters match a specialist's own tagging on one past course?
Will the works council agree to group-level reporting only?

tasks.short: Design onboarding and training programmes per site and job, with managers and the works council.

today.trigger: New site process, high early turnover, a new role, or the yearly training plan.
steps: Talk to managers and new hires to find needs
Design the programme flow and choose formats
Agree budget and planning with the HR Director
Present training policy changes to the works council
Coordinate trainers, rooms and Studytube setup
today.time_sinks: Needs interviews, alignment meetings and rewriting designs.

lenses.faster: AI summarises interviews and drafts the programme outline and works council note; design choices stay with the specialist, saving about 25%.
lenses.autonomous: Little runs alone; a request in the intake list starts a draft needs summary from AFAS data and interview notes.
lenses.ambitious: A week-one onboarding programme for flex workers per site, a group served for the first time, tied to the North Star of hires still productive at day 90.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses formatting programme documents; the specialist wants more time with managers on what good looks like.
lenses.options: Two or three programme designs (classroom-heavy, on-the-job buddy, blended) with cost and shift impact let the HR Director choose.
lenses.altitude: The specialist decides programme design for hire-to-productive and presents it to the works council; more expert.
reach: HR Business Partner: onboarding parts of workforce plans
Recruiter: onboarding handover from offer to day one

tasks.human_edge: Understanding site culture, persuading managers, and gaining works council consent.
tasks.pattern_why: Design is judgment and negotiation; AI helps research and draft, the specialist leads.

in_practice.trigger: A programme request or an early-turnover signal in Power BI.
steps: Model summarises interviews and AFAS turnover data
Model drafts two or three programme options
Specialist chooses and adapts with managers
Specialist drafts works council note with AI help
in_practice.human_gate: HR Director approves; works council consents to training policy changes (WOR 27(1)(f)).

evidence.claim: Training policy needs works council consent under WOR 27(1)(f).
No opened source shows a course cutting time-to-skill.

risks: Generic designs that ignore site reality
Works council consent missed, making a policy void
research_questions: Which onboarding elements correlate with 90-day retention at Noordhaven today?
How long does a programme design take from request to launch now?
Would agencies co-fund flex worker onboarding?

tasks.short: Compare classroom, on-the-job and e-learning on cost, effect and travel between Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.

today.trigger: Budget round, a provider contract renewal, or a complaint about lost shift hours.
steps: Collect provider invoices, hours lost and travel costs
Pull completion and pass rates from Studytube
Build a cost comparison in Excel
Ask learners and managers via a survey
Recommend a mode to the HR Director
drudgery: Collecting invoices and hours by hand
Rebuilding the cost model each time
today.time_sinks: Gathering cost data from AFAS and agency invoices.

lenses.faster: A standing cost model pulls AFAS ledger lines, hours and Studytube results; AI drafts the survey and summary, saving about 35%.
lenses.autonomous: Contract renewal dates trigger a refreshed cost comparison; the specialist judges effect and recommends.
lenses.ambitious: Delivery mode chosen per course every quarter rather than once a year, a decision made far more often; demand would grow modestly.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses hunting invoices; the specialist wants more time on what actually works for shift workers.
lenses.options: Scenarios (all classroom, blended, on-site trainer per site) with cost, shift hours lost and travel CO2 change the decision itself.
lenses.altitude: The specialist decides delivery mode per course within budget and advises on provider contracts; more expert in cost and effect.
reach: FP&A Analyst: training budget forecasts; needs budgeting basics
Controller: training cost allocation per site

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a cheaper mode still builds real skill, especially for practical safety training.
tasks.pattern_why: The cost model is deterministic but the evaluation of effect is judgment; the specialist leads.

steps: Cost model refreshes from AFAS and Studytube
Model drafts learner survey and summarises responses
Specialist runs scenarios
Specialist recommends to HR Director
in_practice.human_gate: HR Director decides mode and budget.

risks: Cost wins over effect for practical skills
Survey data too thin for conclusions
research_questions: Are training costs coded consistently in AFAS ledgers?
Do e-learning pass rates for safety refreshers match classroom ones?
How many shift hours does classroom training cost per year?

tasks.short: Keep up with L&D, AI Act and CAO developments by reading articles, newsletters and attending events.

today.trigger: Weekly reading time, newsletters, or a new law or CAO change.
steps: Scan newsletters and LinkedIn
Read articles and reports
Attend webinars and events
Share relevant items with HR colleagues
drudgery: Scanning many newsletters for little value

lenses.faster: A weekly digest summarises sources with links; the specialist reads the originals that matter, saving about 35%.
lenses.autonomous: A weekly run collects and summarises; the specialist decides what to share.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly briefing on AI Act Article 4 duties and CAO training rules for the HR team and works council, a new service to named internal customers.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses scanning newsletters; the specialist wants more time reading deeply.
lenses.altitude: The specialist becomes the in-house source on AI literacy duties; more expert.
reach: HR Director: AI literacy policy briefings

tasks.human_edge: Judging what applies to Noordhaven and reading critically; summaries must not replace learning.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns a batch of sources into a checkable digest with links.

steps: Collect items from chosen sources
Model summarises with links
Specialist reads key originals
Specialist shares notes in Teams
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist checks claims against original sources before sharing.

evidence.claim: Delegating to AI lowered mastery scores 17%; asking for explanations kept more.
AI literacy duty applies since 2025 and is supervised from 2 August 2026, without a set level.

risks: Summaries replace real learning
Wrong legal summaries shared
research_questions: Which sources does the team actually use?
Do digests change any L&D decision within a quarter?

tasks.short: Review course materials from external trainers and internal experts for accuracy, level and fit.

today.trigger: A provider or internal expert submits materials.
steps: Read outlines, slides and handouts
Check against SOPs, CAO and safety rules
Check reading level and language
Send feedback and approve

lenses.faster: A model checks materials against a checklist and SOPs and flags issues; the specialist reviews flags and decides, saving about 45%.
lenses.autonomous: Submission triggers a checklist review; the specialist approves.
lenses.ambitious: Every provider's materials checked before each run, not only at contract start, a decision made far more often.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses line-by-line checks; the specialist wants more time coaching instructors.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the quality standard for providers; more expert.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: provider contract quality clauses

tasks.human_edge: Judging teaching quality and safety accuracy; the safety lead signs safety content.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call checks materials against a fixed checklist, producing checkable flags.

in_practice.trigger: Materials uploaded to SharePoint review folder.
steps: Model checks against checklist, SOPs and reading level
Specialist reviews flags
Safety lead signs safety content
Specialist sends feedback
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves; safety lead signs safety content.

evidence.claim: MHR uses an agent to check reading level with a person reviewing.

risks: False comfort from missed errors
Outdated SOPs used as reference
research_questions: How accurate are model flags on three past reviews?
Are SOPs in SharePoint current?

role.altitude: From producing courses to owning the competence record and the Article 4 AI literacy measures file for 1,200 staff, deciding certification priorities and programme measures with site managers.
reach: HR Administrator: certificate data and onboarding packs
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: training dashboards in Power BI
HR Business Partner: coaching team leads on absence conversations
role.ceiling_note: Practical safety training, works council consent, and judgment on site culture stay human; content and admin hours shrink most, roughly 30% of role time overall.
skills_to_grow: AI Act and AVG knowledge for learning data
role.ambitious_version: Every shift worker and flex worker certified and onboarded before their first shift at all three sites, measured against 90-day retention.
